questions.question: Why is a verification layer essential in a voice-to-code pipeline?
choices: It makes the pipeline look more professional
Generated code can have subtle bugs that must be caught before applying to the editor
It's required by the STT model
questions.explanation: Code generation models produce code that often looks correct but can contain subtle bugs, missing edge cases, or incorrect logic. A verification layer tests the code against sample inputs before it's inserted into the editor.

questions.question: What is 'design before building' in the context of voice-to-code?
choices: Writing the code first, then designing the architecture
Mapping out each pipeline layer and its interactions before writing implementation code
Using a design tool like Figma to mock up the UI
questions.explanation: Voice-to-code has multiple interacting layers (STT, intent parsing, code gen, verification, application). Designing the full pipeline first prevents discovering fundamental architectural problems midway through implementation.

questions.question: What is a common STT error in voice-to-code systems?
choices: Technical terms like 'sort' can be misheard as 'short' or other similar words
STT only works with American English accents
questions.explanation: Speech-to-text systems can misrecognize words, especially technical terms that sound similar to common words. This is why confidence checks and confirmation steps are essential design elements.
